# Slipstream UI - AI-First React Component Library

## Overview
Slipstream UI is an AI-first React component library designed for AI-assisted development. Every component ships a machine-readable COMPONENT_MANIFEST so coding agents like Claude, Cursor, and Copilot can generate correct UI the first time.

## Key Differentiator
AI reads the spec, not the source. Each component includes a COMPONENT_MANIFEST JSON file containing:
- Component metadata (id, name, tier)
- Design intent and purpose
- Full prop schema with types, defaults, and constraints
- Usage examples (good and anti-patterns)
- Accessibility requirements
- Content guidelines for AI text generation
- Composition rules

## Quick Start
```bash
npx slipstream-ui@latest init
# or
pnpm add @slipstream-ui/core @slipstream-ui/ai
```

## Package Structure
- @slipstream-ui/core - Base atoms and molecules (Button, Input, Badge, Avatar, Spinner, Select, Toast, Dialog)
- @slipstream-ui/ai - AI interaction components (Message, Conversation, PromptInput, Reasoning, ToolCall, Sources, Suggestions, ChainThought, StreamingIndicator, Attachment, MessageActions, CommandPalette)
- @slipstream-ui/themes - Theming system with createTheme() and presets
- @slipstream-ui/mcp-server - MCP server for AI agents
- @slipstream-ui/cli - CLI tool for installation and management

## Core components (@slipstream-ui/core) — 42

- Accordion — Collapsible content sections with ARIA accordion semantics and keyboard navigation
- Alert — Inline alert for status messages with semantic variants (destructive, success, warning, info)
- Autocomplete — Type-ahead input following the HTML autocomplete model: any value is allowed while matching suggestions appear in a keyboard-navigable listbox.
- Avatar — A user profile image component with fallback support and accessible image loading
- Badge — A small status indicator component for displaying tags, counts, or status information
- Block — Semantic container (div by default, swappable element) — the structural counterpart to Text (p).
- Breadcrumb — Navigation breadcrumb trail with links and current-page indicator
- Button — A clickable button component with variants for different visual styles and sizes
- ButtonGroup — Joins buttons into one segmented control: adjacent borders collapse, middle corners square off, and only the outer corners stay rounded — a single outline around the group.
- Card — A content container with header, body, and footer sections for grouping related information
- Checkbox — A native checkbox input styled to match the design system, plus CheckboxGroup for grouping related options under an accessible legend
- DataTable — Config-driven table: one component plus a columns config that owns shape, sorting, pagination, and row interaction.
- Dialog — Accessible modal dialog with focus trapping, escape-to-close and focus restoration
- Drawer — Edge sheet for secondary flows: slides from any side (sm/md/lg), with Dialog-grade modal semantics (portal, focus trap, Escape, focus restoration).
- Fieldset — Groups related form controls in a native fieldset with a legend, optional description, and an error slot.
- Flex / FlexItem — Typed flexbox container (direction/align/justify/wrap/gap) with FlexItem for per-child grow/shrink/basis controls.
- Form — Semantic form element with even-spacing layouts: stacked (default), bordered card, or inline row — native submit and validation untouched.
- FormField — Label + control + hint/error in one unit with htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid wiring applied automatically.
- FormLayout — Groups form fields with even, tokenized spacing: vertical stack, horizontal row, or 1-4 column grid, optionally as a semantic fieldset.
- Grid / GridItem — Typed CSS grid with column counts per breakpoint (literal utilities that survive purging), auto-fit min-column mode, and GridItem spans.
- Heading — Semantic heading (h1-h6) with a safe default scale and an optional visual-size override.
- Input — A text input field with support for various input types and standard HTML input attributes
- InputGroup — Composite input shell with flush left/right addons (icons, units, buttons) behind one outer outline; the nested field sheds its own border so the group reads as a single control.
- Label — An accessible form label that associates with its control
- List / ListItem — Semantic list (ul/li) for rows of related items: settings, results, nav — with leading/trailing slots, selection, and pressable rows.
- Menu — Dropdown menu with keyboard navigation, typeahead, and ARIA menu semantics
- Pagination — Numeric pagination with prev/next, ellipsis, and aria-current on the active page
- Popover — Floating panel anchored to a trigger with interactive content, closing on outside click and Escape
- Progress — A determinate progress bar with role=progressbar and exact value semantics
- Radio — Native radio buttons grouped for mutually exclusive choices, with an accessible fieldset/legend wrapper
- Search — Select-with-search: type to filter a full-width dropdown of options, or arrow through the full set from an empty query.
- Select — Accessible select primitive built on the native select element with controlled and uncontrolled modes
- Separator — A visual divider between content blocks, decorative or semantic
- Skeleton — A loading placeholder that mirrors the shape of upcoming content
- Spinner — Indeterminate loading indicator with accessible status semantics.
- Switch — A toggle switch for binary settings, with role=switch and aria-checked
- Table — Semantic data table with headers, body, footer, and accessible caption
- Tabs — Tabbed content container with ARIA tablist semantics and keyboard navigation
- Text — Semantic paragraph text with a controlled type scale; renders a real p (or span with inline).
- Textarea — A multi-line text input styled to match Input, wrapping the native textarea
- Toast — Accessible app-level notifications announced through a polite live region, with auto-dismiss, stacking and optional actions
- Tooltip — Hover/focus tooltip with aria-describedby association, delay, and Escape dismissal

## AI components (@slipstream-ui/ai) — 17

- Attachment / AttachmentList — File chips for prompts and messages. `Attachment` renders one file; `AttachmentList` renders a wrapping row. Display-only: upload and file-system logic stay in the consumer.
- Branch — Variant navigation for branched messages: previous/next arrows with an N/M position indicator.
- ChainThought — Displays ordered reasoning steps with status indicators.
- CodeBlock — Syntax-highlighted code block with language label and copy-to-clipboard button.
- CommandPalette — Cmd+K style command palette with lexical search, sectioned results and full keyboard navigation
- Confirmation — Human-in-the-loop approval gate for agent actions. Pauses execution until the user approves or rejects.
- Conversation — A container for displaying a list of chat messages with auto-scroll and loading states
- InlineCitation — Perplexity-style inline citation chip that reveals the source title and snippet on hover or keyboard focus.
- Message — A chat message component that displays messages from users, assistants, or system prompts with optional avatars
- MessageActions — Feedback toolbar for an AI response: copy to clipboard, thumbs up/down rating, and regenerate. Every action is a callback; the component holds no conversation state.
- PromptInput — A textarea input for entering chat prompts with auto-resize, keyboard shortcuts, and send button
- Reasoning — A collapsible component for displaying AI reasoning steps and chain-of-thought processes
- Response — Streaming-optimized markdown renderer for AI responses with GFM support, streaming-safe repair of incomplete syntax, and highlighted code blocks with copy.
- Source / Sources — Displays citations and references for an AI response. `Source` renders a single citation; `Sources` renders a numbered list with an overflow count.
- StreamingIndicator — Shows that an AI response is currently streaming.
- Suggestions — Displays clickable follow-up prompts for AI interactions.
- ToolCall — A component for displaying AI tool/function calls with status, arguments, and results
<!-- generated:ai:end -->

## Registry
Static manifest registry served from the docs site:
- GET /registry/all.json - index of every component with id, name, tier, description
- GET /registry/<id>.json - full COMPONENT_MANIFEST plus a shadcn-compatible installer payload with embedded file contents
- Install source copies: npx shadcn@latest add https://slipstreamui.com/registry/<id>.json

## Canonical markdown docs for agents
- GET /llm/index.md - library overview and component index (complete, generated from manifests)
- GET /llm/components/<id>.md - full per-component reference generated from its manifest
Prefer these over HTML pages when generating code.

## MCP Server
The MCP server provides tools for AI agents:
- list_components - Query available components with filters
- get_component_manifest - Get full COMPONENT_MANIFEST for a specific component
- get_usage_examples - Get usage examples, composition rules, and anti-patterns
- validate_usage - Validate generated JSX against a component manifest before emitting; detects hallucinated props and missing required props

## Production UX notes
- Components are stateless; consumers own thread/conversation state
- Streaming: isStreaming/streamingMessageId render cursors; Response repairs incomplete markdown automatically
- Accessibility: aria-busy during streams, polite completion announcements, reduced-motion variants on animations
- Empty transcripts render a configurable welcome state with starter prompts
- Failed generations render inline error cards with retry callbacks (Message error/onRetry)
- PromptInput supports compound primitives, drag-drop/paste attachments with constraints, dictation, and status-aware submit

## Documentation
Full documentation at https://slipstreamui.com/docs

## For AI Agents
When generating UI code:
1. Query the MCP server for component manifests
2. Read prop schemas and usage examples
3. Follow content guidelines for text generation
4. Respect composition rules and anti-patterns
5. Ensure accessibility requirements are met

## Example Usage
```tsx
import { Button } from '@slipstream-ui/core'
import { Message, Conversation, PromptInput } from '@slipstream-ui/ai'

function ChatApp() {
  const [messages, setMessages] = useState([
    { id: '1', role: 'user', content: 'Hello!' }
  ])

  return (
    <div>
      <Conversation messages={messages} />
      <PromptInput onSubmit={(text) => setMessages([...messages, { id: Date.now(), role: 'user', content: text }])} />
    </div>
  )
}
```
